title: HC Mike LaFleur Press Conference: October 23 | Week 7 vs. Denver Broncos
headline: Jeremiyah Love and Jon Gaines are out Sunday; Hayden Conner steps in for Gaines, and Budda Baker and Darius Robinson are being monitored.
summary: LaFleur said Jeremiyah Love, Jon Gaines and one other player (name garbled in captions) will miss Sunday. Gaines suffered an ankle injury in practice and Hayden Conner will replace him. LaFleur said there has been no discussion of placing Love on IR. Budda Baker hasn't practiced this week, but LaFleur expects him to be fine, with a final check planned for game day. Darius Robinson was downgraded to limited, and LaFleur said he is feeling better and will be evaluated up to kickoff. LaFleur also described the Denver defense as well coached and talented, with no weak link, and said Bo Nix and the Broncos offense have been good despite a rough statistical start. On the backfield, he said Tyler Allgeier is the smart, protection-capable back used on third downs, while Bam Knight does most of the first- and second-down work. He also said no back should carry 65 to 70 plays a game, so rotation is the plan. LaFleur added that the team is focused on red zone improvement this week and wants to play well at home for Larry Fitzgerald's halftime honors.

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Media Availability | Friday, October 23rd | Press Conference
headline: Khalil Herbert is expected to be elevated to the active roster with Brian Robinson out, while AJ Terrell and Avieon Terrell remain questionable for the 49ers game.
summary: Stefanski said AJ Terrell has looked better and has worked hard since he has been out, but the staff will assess him over the next 48 hours. He hoped at least a couple of the questionable players (including the Terrells) would be available Sunday, but said medical clearance depends on how they respond through the week. He confirmed that Khalil Herbert is moving up to the active roster with Brian Robinson out. He called Kendall Daniels' progress a huge blessing, noting he is doing better overall and continuing to put himself in a good spot. On the 49ers, he said Brock Purdy stays in the heart of the pocket and uses the B gaps to escape, and that San Francisco is facing the same availability issues in the NFL's week-to-week grind. He stressed that backups must prepare as starters. Stefanski also talked about play-calling, saying bad outcomes are often about execution and defensive looks rather than the call alone, and that the staff agrees on the Sunday call sheet. He expects San Francisco's blitz and coverage rates to be decided during the game.

title: Jesse Minter Discusses Lamar Jackson, Tavius Robinson
headline: Lamar Jackson's status for Sunday is undecided after a limited Friday practice; Zion Young and Ethan Burke are set for bigger roles with Tavius Robinson out for the season.
summary: Minter opened by announcing that Tavius Robinson has a season-ending injury and will miss the rest of the year, though he declined to give details. Jaylinn Hawkins will miss this game, and the staff is still gathering information on his longer-term status. Asked about Lamar Jackson, Minter said Jackson is still working through an injury and was limited in practice, though he got a good amount of work in over the last couple of days. The final call will be based on how Jackson feels, how effective he can be, and how he responds, with the staff willing to wait as long as necessary, and Minter said there is no clear threshold. Minter said the secondary has depth to cover Hawkins' absence, with Chidobe Awuzie possibly seeing more snaps, K'Von Wallace and Keondre Jackson ready to step in, and Kyle Hamilton able to move around. He praised Zion Young and Ethan Burke as more experienced players who understand the physicality and are ready for more snaps. On Robinson, Minter said he feels for him and that the group must keep playing at its level without him. Minter said he does not believe the Robinson injury is a long-term concern beyond the season.

title: Dave Canales: 'We're excited for a championship opportunity'
headline: Monroe Freeling looked great in practice after his knee injury and could take on a bigger role. Thomas Incoom is out, which opens a special-teams-and-backup RB spot that Trevor Etienne may fill if he is activated.
summary: Canales said the team is excited for the division game against Tampa Bay at Bank of America Stadium and sees it as a real championship opportunity. He called Monroe Freeling's week excellent, saying he looked great coming back from his knee injury and has a lot of energy, and that he will have a chance to help the team. He declined to say whether Rasheed Walker and another tackle will keep starting for now, citing possibilities still being weighed. On the run game, he admitted establishing it early has been the group's main challenge, noting the Eagles' stout front in the prior game and the importance of consistency and efficiency over explosive runs. On Baker Mayfield, Canales expected him to start in a custom glove and said he was not surprised given Mayfield's toughness, pointing to a similar Seattle situation with Russell Wilson. He said the Bucs' offense under Zac Robinson mixes concepts from his Atlanta days with what Liam Coen brought, and that Bucky Irving fits into how they get the ball out. On the running back room, Canales said Trevor Etienne has emerged on special teams and that activating a third back on game day is a possibility. Thomas Incoom is out, so Nick Hampton and others will fill his leadership and special-teams role. On injuries, JK and Jonathon Brooks are rehabbing well, but both still need to pass violent change-of-direction work before opening up. Jackson Kuwatch is on IR with a season-ending surgery.

title: Ben Johnson on Bears' Thursday night victory over Patriots | Press Conference
headline: Ben Johnson praised Luther Burden III, Colston Loveland, and Rome Odunze for big pass-catching games and said Cole Kmet's knee injury didn't look good, with an update due Friday.
summary: Johnson said the Bears were proud of a physical 30-24 win over New England that took all 60 minutes, calling it a good team and a short-week grind. He credited all three phases, including a Jack Sanborn end-zone interception and the onside kick recovery. He said the pass catchers stepped up, with Luther Burden III providing an early spark, Colston Loveland making plays in the middle, and Rome Odunze coming through late. Johnson praised special teams, including strong kickoff coverage and a late 58-yard field goal that sealed the game. On the quarterback, he said Caleb Williams had a good night with explosive plays and accurate throws that extended drives, noting that 300 yards and a couple of touchdowns is a good night. He said the team had to work to get its running game going early. On injuries, he said Cole Kmet was ruled out with a knee injury, that he didn't think it looked good, and that more information would come the next day, and he also mentioned an unnamed toe injury that would be updated then. He said the team recovered well on a short week and kept a normal game plan. He praised Drake Maye for his play and said Williams's comfort grew with two straight weeks of finding open receivers.

topics.detail: Johnson called kickoff coverage phenomenal and said a kicker made a 58-yard field goal at the end that sealed the win. He also mentioned a missed earlier kick that was followed by a make, and that the team's special teams have been strong almost every week.

Johnson praised New England's Drake Maye, saying he is outstanding and hard to contain, and that the Patriots' quick outlet passes kept the Bears' defense on its toes. The Bears gave up a late first-half touchdown that Johnson said could have been stopped with a better rally to the ball.

Johnson said the team focused on recovery on a short week, that many players were playing through injuries, and that the game plan was largely unchanged from normal. He stressed that the team's resilience comes from practicing through adversity in the spring and training camp.

title: Ben Johnson reviews Thursday's victory, gives update on Cole Kmet | Press Conference
headline: Cole Kmet has a serious knee injury and goes on IR today; Sam Roush and Colston Loveland should see bigger roles, and Luther Burden III is the emerging playmaker.
summary: Johnson said the team showed resolve winning Thursday on a short week and that the staff deserves credit for the preparation. The coming weekend is a mini bye that gives the staff time to evaluate personnel and scheme. He confirmed Cole Kmet's knee injury is serious and that Kmet will be placed on IR later Friday. Johnson praised Kmet as a leader and said the tight-end group will need to step up, pointing to practice-squad development as depth. He said Luther Burden III is elite with the ball in his hands and is being used more in intermediate routes, though the team has not yet targeted him over the top this year. Johnson also said Sam Roush's rep count will likely rise, and Colston Loveland's target share has grown, with a couple of drops against the Patriots he is expected to rebound from. On the offensive line, Theo Benedet was called solid at left tackle, and Jonah Jackson was described as playing through the week with a tough attitude. Caleb Williams was praised for speeding up his progressions and escaping pressure, though the offense still has pre-snap and holding penalties to clean up.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference : October 23rd, 2026
headline: Mason Graham is back from injury, Dylan Sampson is expected to return Sunday after his knee issue, and Grant Delpit's protocol clearance is expected Friday.
summary: Monken opened by saying a Denzel was added to the injury report with a finger problem, but he couldn't say how it happened and expects that player to play Sunday. He was glad to have Mason Graham back, saying the injury was less serious than feared and that Graham was off to a strong start. Grant Delpit remains in the concussion protocol and is expected to be cleared around tomorrow. He credited the team's toughness and connectedness for players pushing to return from injuries. On the running game, he said getting Dylan Sampson and Quinshon Judkins back together should help, though the offense still needs work. He praised Carson Schwesinger's preparation and quick reactions, and said Sampson had taken another step forward in his knee rehab and is a big threat in the screen game. Monken said the offense's slow starts come from scheme, coaching, and execution, not excuses, and that the team is 4-2 and still under construction. He also said he's comfortable letting coordinators run the defense and special teams during games, and that Tennessee has good players and coaches on a young roster.

title: HC Sean Payton on the importance of stacking wins: ‘We have to be ascending [and] improving’
headline: Jonah Coleman is returning from a four-week absence and will be monitored on pitch count, while Bo Nix's rushing is not a priority for Denver.
summary: Payton said the current injury protocol lets players stay in shape and train, which has helped a returning player. He downplayed a bigger role for Bo Nix as a runner, saying some designed runs will happen organically and that it is not near the top of the list. On fullbacks, he said most teams use a tight end to do that job, that Nate Adkins could fill those roles, and that he prefers a true fullback without sacrificing a better player. He called Zach Allen's tape fantastic and credited rotation and extra rest for his lowest snap percentage of Payton's tenure, which he said is purposeful given his energy. He praised Ja'Quan McMillian's high level of play and instincts, and said he is a good find in a defense that values a nickel's ability to get the ball. On Coleman's return from injury, Payton said he watches pitch count closely for first games back after a month or more. He said he would not announce the Cardinals starting lineup, and he framed the week around Arizona with a focus on not looking ahead. He said the team needs to keep ascending and improving, and that depth at positions like corner has helped them absorb injuries.

title: Campbell on preparing for Green Bay
headline: Cade Mays moves into the starting lineup over Juice Scruggs, and Brian Branch is ready to play Sunday vs. Green Bay.
summary: Dan Campbell said Brian Branch is ready to play and the staff has a good idea of his role, though they will manage his workload. He addressed Sam LaPorta's recent comments on Pardon My Take, saying the team is 'all good' and the matter will not be a distraction. Campbell explained that Cade Mays was brought in for specific mental and physical traits, and that the move is part of working toward the best five on the line, with Juice Scruggs still expected to play a role. He called Jordan Love's play excellent, noting Love's 59% completion rate is misleading given his deep-ball production and how well the protection has held the last two games. He praised the Packers defense as a physical unit that plays together, creates disruption, and has forced seven takeaways in two weeks. Campbell said Sunday is a big test after the Cardinals win, which he called Detroit's best game, and that the team needs to play cleaner. He was excited about DeAndre Carter's speed and ball skills as a returner and special teams piece. Campbell closed by saying he would not keep answering questions about LaPorta's comments.

title: Matt LaFleur on Jordon Riley: 'The work he puts in does not go unnoticed by anybody'
headline: Zaire Franklin is out Sunday vs. the Lions with a shin injury the coach says isn't long-term; Ty'Ron Hopper and Isaiah McDuffie get the extra work, and Josh Jacobs is on track but limited in practice.
summary: LaFleur said the Lions' Ford Field crowd has become a hostile environment and he expects a tough road game Sunday. Linebacker Zaire Franklin took a knee to the shin in a collision and will miss this game. LaFleur said it isn't a broken bone and he doesn't expect a long-term issue, though they are still working through it. He expressed confidence in Isaiah McDuffie and Ty'Ron Hopper to step in, and praised Hopper for maximizing his opportunities and developing well since training camp, calling this a chance for him to get more reps. Asked about a defensive lineman who was injured last year, LaFleur praised his size, energy and work ethic but did not name him in a way that matches the roster. On Josh Jacobs, LaFleur said he believes Jacobs is on track to play, pending how he feels and his own confidence, with those decisions coming after practice. He also confirmed Jacobs was limited in practice but said he will participate.

headline: Jordan Mason is listed as questionable but will practice fully all week, and the coach expects him to be available vs. the Colts; Josh Oliver's absence remains a significant loss.

He said Jordan Mason will practice fully all week and is technically questionable, but no other player will carry a game designation, so the roster is healthier. He is optimistic Mason will be available. O'Connell praised the run game's effort and blocking, including Kyler Murray's athleticism and receivers' blocking, and said Mason's return paired with Aaron Jones will be a positive, since Jones has carried a heavy workload. On the defensive side, he credited Ryan Nielsen's one-on-one teaching, especially pre-snap communication, and discussed how the Vikings' defense can disguise coverages and fronts. He said Kyler Murray reads those looks well. He also discussed how split-safety shells are suppressing explosive runs. Finally, he said losing Josh Oliver has been a big blow, since Oliver brought physicality and run blocking and complemented T.J. Hockenson. The team is adapting with more versatility, including Gavin Bartholomew, Ben Yurosek, Max Bredeson, and Caleb Tiernan in a jumbo package.

title: WATCH: Mike McCarthy Media Availability (Oct. 23)
headline: DeShon Elliott's return is close: his activation will be decided after Saturday's practice, while T.J. Watt's calf is not seen as a concern for Sunday.
summary: McCarthy said the team's plan for the Paris trip was to activate players after the long flight, and he wished they had stopped at the walkthrough site. He described an adjusted sleep and schedule plan to manage the time change, with extra sleep before the trip and a normal schedule after 6 p.m. local time. He called the first-ever NFL game in Paris a big deal and said he expects a tough, important matchup against the Saints. title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald Gives Final Updates Ahead Of Week 7 vs. Chiefs
headline: Charbonnet, Surratt and Drake Thomas are out vs. the Chiefs; Anthony Bradford will play the full game and Tyrice Knight keeps expanding his role.
summary: Macdonald opened with the injury report: Zach Charbonnet, Chazz Surratt and Drake Thomas are out for Sunday, while Nick Emmanwori (hip, new at Friday's practice), Connor O'Toole and Drew Lock (elbow) are questionable. He said Charbonnet has had no setbacks and is progressing as planned, with a return to be evaluated next week. Anthony Bradford is expected to play the entire game, and Macdonald said his return restores continuity on the starting five next to Abraham Lucas. Jadarian Price is progressing well, with his practice window possibly opening next week. Elijah Arroyo had surgery and is expected to miss the rest of the season, so the staff will have to find ways to replace his skill set. On defense, Tyrice Knight has filled in seamlessly for Drake Thomas with a different style, and Macdonald said Knight deserves the playing time. Macdonald said the tight end room is not measured only by catches and that the group is the engine of the offense, but the staff can find more opportunities for them. He also praised AJ Barner's leadership and Brady Russell's special teams play, and he credited players for organizing cross-positional meetings on their own.

summary: Bowles said Baker Mayfield looked good in practice and appears ready to play. Bowles described Mayfield's week as normal and said he was a full participant on Wednesday. The coach said a player named Luke, whose exact identity is unclear in the captions, will not play Sunday, is still in the protocol, and is listed as doubtful. He confirmed that Antoine Winfield Jr. is out and said no one else besides Luke and Winfield is out. Benjamin Morrison and Sean Tucker, who were out last week, have practiced all week. On Emeka Egbuka, Bowles said the team could not identify the specific play that led to delayed-onset concussion symptoms after a hit following a middle route, despite reviewing the tape. Bowles said the lineup call between two options will be made at game time and he would not announce it yet. He also said the team's focus is on winning Sunday's divisional game against Carolina.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Saleh says Alontae Taylor is working nickel while still able to play corner, Marcus Harris is being trained outside, and Cody Barton has earned more snaps.
summary: Saleh opened by saying injuries are trending the right way, with no one ruled out yet and a few items still to be cleared that day. He said the team has moved past last week's off-field distractions and that the focus is on Sunday. He acknowledged the franchise's recent struggles, noting the team's 13-51 record over the last 64 games, and framed a two-game winning streak as a step forward. On offense he said short, screen, medium, and deep passing all need to improve, along with third-down and red-zone scoring, and blamed a mix of missed throws, drops, and tipped balls rather than one fix. On defense, Alontae Taylor is getting nickel reps and has responded with energy, though Saleh said he still needs to earn the job and can still play corner. Saleh said Marcus Harris is playing well at nickel, is being trained outside as well, and that the nickel spot needs depth after Marcus went down briefly in the game. Saleh described how players react to reduced roles, saying Cody Barton has earned more opportunities and the right to play, and that Tony Adams wants more field time, likely once Kevin Winston returns. Saleh also said a returning player who had been out is excited to be back and looked good in practice, though the coach did not name him in the answer.
